primary_entered: every raw row (all 120 individual fish, 60 per feed)
stated_N: 120 measured fish (60 standard, 60 algal_oil); t = 13.345, df = 118
label: POSITIVE
evidence: Feed was assigned to whole cages (10 cages) but analysis.py runs stats.ttest_ind on all 120 per-fish rows with df = 118, and the report states the sample size entered into the test as 120 measured fish, with no cage-level or dependence-aware component anywhere.
rowwise_role: It is the sole and primary inferential result; the report's headline p = 2.5e-25 and 95% CI come from it.

primary_entered: every raw row (all 336 person-mornings, 168 per arm)
label: POSITIVE
evidence: Volunteers were randomised as whole people (24 units, 14 mornings each), yet analysis.py comments that 'the analysed sample size is the number of mornings' and runs Welch ttest_ind on all 336 rows, which the report reports as n = 336 with df = 317.2 and no random effect, cluster method, or per-person reduction.
rowwise_role: It is the only inferential test and supplies the headline result (p = 3.0e-92) and clinical conclusion.

primary_entered: every raw row (all 60 counting slides, 30 per drench)
stated_N: 60 counts analysed (30 per drench); t = 12.301, df = 38.4
label: POSITIVE
evidence: The three rows per goat are laboratory re-counts of one faecal sample from the same animal, but analysis.py states 'each counting slide entered as its own observation' and runs Welch ttest_ind on all 60 rows, giving df = 38.4 rather than the 20 randomised goats, with no goat-level averaging or mixed model.
rowwise_role: It is the primary and only inferential test; the efficacy conclusion and drench recommendation rest on its p = 6.76e-15.

primary_entered: every raw row (all 80 logged classrooms, 40 per group)
stated_N: 80 classroom records (40 upgraded, 40 unupgraded); t = 16.001, df = 70.39
label: POSITIVE
evidence: The ventilation upgrade was installed building-wide across 16 buildings, but analysis.py passes all 80 classroom rows into Welch ttest_ind ('one observation per logged classroom record') and the report analyses n = 80 with df = 70.39, with no building-level aggregation or clustering adjustment.
rowwise_role: It is the sole inferential result and drives the estates board recommendation (p = 3.8e-25).

primary_entered: every raw row (all 84 bin-visits, 42 per atmosphere)
stated_N: 84 firmness records (42 per group); t = 2.903, df = 82
label: POSITIVE
evidence: Atmosphere was assigned to 14 whole bins each sampled six times over the season, yet analysis.py runs stats.ttest_ind on all 84 firmness records ('Every firmness record ... enters the comparison as its own observation') and reports df = 82, ignoring both the per-bin repeats and the storage_week time structure.
rowwise_role: It is the primary and only inferential test, supplying the reported p = 0.0047 and the storage recommendation.

primary_entered: every raw row (all 120 measured leaves, 60 per treatment)
label: POSITIVE
evidence: Canopy treatment is a property of the shrub (20 shrubs, 6 leaves each), but analysis.py states 'Every measured leaf enters the comparison as a separate observation' and runs Welch ttest_ind on all 120 leaf rows with df = 114.58, with no shrub-level mean, random effect, or cluster method.
rowwise_role: It is the only inferential test and supplies the headline p = 9.3e-36 and the agroforestry interpretation.

primary_entered: one value per unit (each rat's mean discrimination_index over its 8 runs, 18 values)
source_file: data.csv, reduced in-script by reduce_to_animals() before testing
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: analysis.py reduces each rat's eight runs to that rat's single mean before any comparison and runs Welch ttest_ind on the 18 per-animal values, and the report states the sample size as 18 rats and warns that counting each run separately would inflate the sample size.
rowwise_role: No row-level (run-level) two-sample test exists anywhere in the code; run-level values appear only in descriptive printouts.

primary_entered: every raw row, which here is also one value per unit (40 farms, one yield each)
stated_N: 40 farms (20 per seed group); t = 9.030, df = 37.88
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: The design is genuinely one row per farm (40 rows, 40 distinct farm_id values, verified in the CSV), and analysis.py exits with an error unless rows equal distinct farms, so the row-level Welch t-test is by construction a unit-level test.
rowwise_role: It is the primary inferential test, but it is not pseudoreplication because a row is a farm; the report explicitly notes rows, farms, and independent units are all the same 40.

primary_entered: a model with unit-level random effects (linear mixed model, fgm_ng_per_g ~ husbandry_group with a random intercept per cat, REML), plus a 24-cat-mean t-test cross-check
source_file: shelter_cat_fgm.csv (all 144 rows fed to the mixed model with cat_ref as the grouping factor)
stated_N: 24 cats / 144 samples; contrast -63.25 ng/g, SE 11.22, z = -5.635, p = 1.75e-08
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: The primary inferential result is a REML linear mixed model with a per-cat random intercept (ICC 0.785) and the report labels the 144-row t-test a 'Secondary sensitivity check (not the inferential result)' whose p-value 'must not be read as the study result'.
rowwise_role: Explicitly secondary: printed under a 'SECONDARY SENSITIVITY CHECK (NOT the inferential result)' banner with a design-effect explanation of why its p = 1.63e-25 is optimistic.

primary_entered: one value per unit (the 22 rows of route_summary.csv, each route's mean_weekly_count)
stated_N: 22 routes (11 per regime); Welch t = 7.136, df = 17.98
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: two_group_test() is called on the 22-row per-route summary table and the report states 'The inferential test was therefore run on the 22 rows of route_summary.csv ... No inferential test was run on the weekly rows.'
rowwise_role: No test is run on the 396 weekly rows; describe_weekly() only prints ranges, medians and means, labelled 'descriptive, route-weeks are not independent'.

primary_entered: a cluster-aware resampling (hand-written cluster bootstrap resampling whole patients with replacement, 13 per arm, 20000 replicates, on patient mean depths)
source_file: probing_depth.csv, reduced in-script by patient_table() to 26 patient means that the bootstrap resamples
stated_N: 26 randomised patients (13 per arm), 208 index teeth; estimate -0.382 mm, bootstrap SE 0.122, 95% CI -0.615 to -0.139, p = 0.0017
label: NEGATIVE
evidence: The primary result is a patient-level cluster bootstrap and the tooth-level Welch t-test is printed and reported under 'ILLUSTRATIVE CONTRAST ONLY -- NOT A VALID BASIS FOR INFERENCE', with the report stating 'no conclusion rests on them'.
rowwise_role: Explicitly non-inferential illustration used to show how much the naive standard error shrinks (0.051 mm vs the honest 0.122 mm, a 2.39x factor).

primary_entered: one value per unit (the 16 paddock mean herbage values from aggregate_to_paddocks())
